editorial:
Imagine working in a morgue, making dead people look pretty for their funerals, and still feeling like your own love life is a total disaster. That is exactly where you find the main character in this quirky flick. She is struggling to move on from a messy breakup with her ex-girlfriend while dealing with the oddest job imaginable. The vibe is a weird but sweet mix of dark humor and romantic longing. You get a front-row seat to her awkward attempts at dating again, and it feels like hanging out with a friend who has a very strange hobby but a huge heart.

The acting feels natural and the pacing keeps you interested without dragging. While some of the jokes might feel a bit dated since it came out in the nineties, the charm is still there. You will love how it handles the balance between death and new beginnings. If you want to see it in the best quality, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection for those crisp colors. It is a great pick for a low-key movie night when you want something a bit different from the usual rom-coms.
endingExplained: Everything wraps up when the main character finally stops clinging to the past. She realizes that her ex is not the one for her and that she can find happiness on her own terms. After a series of funny and awkward encounters, she learns to love herself and her strange career. The movie ends on a hopeful note, showing her moving forward with a fresh perspective on love and life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves indie romances with a weird twist.
